subject: maths
title: Intro to Trigonometry (SOH-CAH-TOA)
welcome_lead: Time to meet trigonometry — the three ratios sin, cos, tan that link an angle to a triangle's sides.
meta_desc: GCSE Maths Geometry stretch — intro to sine, cosine and tangent ratios with SOH-CAH-TOA on right-angled triangles.
final_note: You now know SOH-CAH-TOA and can use sin, cos and tan to find unknown sides in right-angled triangles.

concepts.def: The longest side, opposite the right angle.
The side directly across from the chosen angle.
The side next to the angle (not the hypotenuse).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Pick an angle θ (theta). Then label the sides:

• Hypotenuse (H): longest side, opposite the 90° corner.
• Opposite (O): the side directly across from θ.
• Adjacent (A): the remaining side, next to θ.

The labels O and A swap if you change which angle you call θ — H stays the same.

Three ratios link the angle to the sides:

SOH   sin θ = O / H
CAH   cos θ = A / H
TOA   tan θ = O / A

Memorise it: Some Old Hippie Caught Another Hippie Tripping On Acid. Cheesy — but it sticks.

Example: right-angled triangle, hypotenuse = 10 cm, and the angle θ = 30°. Find the opposite side.

You have H and want O → use SOH: sin θ = O/H.

So O = H × sin θ = 10 × sin 30° = 10 × 0.5 = 5 cm.

Quick check: sin 30° = 0.5 is a fact worth memorising. Same for cos 60° = 0.5 and tan 45° = 1.

mcqs.q: In a right-angled triangle, which side is the hypotenuse?
options: The side opposite the right angle
The side next to the chosen angle
Any of the two shorter sides

numericals.q: Right-angled triangle: hypotenuse = 8 cm, angle = 30°. Find the opposite side, in cm.
numericals.hint: Use SOH: opposite = hypotenuse × sin(angle). sin 30° = 0.5.

free_texts.q: Mnemonic for the three trig ratios — three letters per ratio. Give the full nine-letter string with no spaces or dashes. (e.g. answer like SOHCAHTOA).
free_texts.hint: Sine = Opp/Hyp, Cos = Adj/Hyp, Tan = Opp/Adj.
